title: Present Roman School: some sins venial by nature—not yet a defined article
source_text: XVIII. Unde est quod Schola Romana hodie communi consensu contrarium statuit, videlicet, quaedam peccata natura sua venialia esse, & non tantum ex Dei misericordia, atque indulgentia: licet istud nondum habeat pro fidei articulo, & re omnino certa & definita.
pass_a_gloss: Whence it is that the Roman School today by common consent establishes the contrary, namely, that certain sins are venial by their own nature, and not only from God’s mercy and indulgence: although it does not yet hold that for an article of faith and a matter altogether certain and defined.
pass_b_english: Today’s Roman consensus: some sins are venial by nature, not merely by mercy.
Le Blanc notes the point is common doctrine, not yet a defined article of faith.
